subject: Unexpected 429s impacting Novagrid - reconciliation & proposed SLA adjustment
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novagrid.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected 429s impacting Novagrid - initial findings and short-term mitigation

Hi Daniel —

First, sorry for the disruption this morning. We saw a spike of 429 responses from our serving layer for your tenant between 08:40–09:05 PST and again intermittently through the morning. We know this impacted your API throughput and caused retries on some of your workers.

Quick summary of what we have so far:
- Scope: a subset of routes used by Novagrid (embedding and chat endpoints) hit an unexpectedly low per-tenant enforcement window due to a configuration mismatch.
- Impact: transient 429s for approximately 3–6% of requests during peak periods; retries caused additional latency spikes for some of your background jobs.
- Current action: we have applied an immediate temporary override to raise the enforcement window for your tenant while we validate the long-term fix.

Next steps we are doing now:
1) Complete the forensic request log export and attach it to this thread (ETA 3 hours).
2) Run reconciliation between tenant->namespace quota mappings and our enforcement table.
3) Propose an action plan that includes a permanent mapping correction, postmortem, and compensation proposal.

I'll loop in Ben and Karthik for the technical details; Evelyn will coordinate credits and SLA items.

If there's additional context on your side (recent traffic patterns, scheduled batch jobs), please send that over — it will speed the root cause work.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0199
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novagrid.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:28:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s impacting Novagrid - initial findings and short-term mitigation

Tessa, thanks for the quick note.

We saw job backlogs in our nightly inference workers and some client SDKs logged 429s starting ~08:45. Impacted systems: realtime-embedder-prod and batch-featurizer.

We paused retries on the batch pipeline around 09:05 which helped, but realtime traffic still had elevated latency. Any temporary override you applied — what's the window and when does it expire?

Also cc'ing our legal ops because we need to track compensation and any contractual SLA impacts.

—Daniel
Director of Integrations, Novagrid
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:02:36 -0800
Subject: RE: Unexpected 429s impacting Novagrid - preliminary technical root cause

Tessa / team —

Preliminary root cause from infra: during an automated config sync last night we applied a namespace->tenant alias update that inadvertently overwrote the per-tenant enforcement key for Novagrid. In our policies there is a fallback that should have preserved the previous mapping, but a logic gap in the sync script caused it to write an empty enforcement window value into the active table for one of Novagrid's namespaces. The enforcement system treats an empty value as the default low window (60s) instead of the tenant-specific 300s value.

Consequence: heavy concurrent traffic from Novagrid that normally fits into the 300s window appeared to exceed the enforcement window and triggered 429s.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Temporary override set to 600s for Novagrid namespace to avoid further 429s while we fix the mapping (applied 10:50 PST).
- Re-run of the sync in dry-run mode to confirm no other tenants were affected.

Fix plan (technical):
1) Roll back the erroneous script change and deploy a validation check to prevent empty enforcement values (ETA: 48 hours).
2) Reconcile historical request logs to ensure no missed requests were double-counted (ETA: 24 hours).
3) Add an alert to surface enforcement-value anomalies earlier.

I'll attach the request logs and a CSV of the tenant->namespace mapping for your review.

-ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novagrid.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s impacting Novagrid - remediation proposal and credit offer

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the quick context. Ben's team confirmed the temporary override is in place and we've validated that realtime latency has returned to baseline for most call types. Below is the proposed remediation and commercial reconciliation: 

Technical remediation (what we'll do in next 48 hours):
- Permanent correction of the tenant->namespace enforcement mapping (non-disruptive).
- Deploy a validation gate on the sync script to reject empty enforcement values.
- Add a heartbeat metric and alert for enforcement value drift.

Customer remediation (what we propose):
- Immediate: we will credit Novagrid for the affected window proportionally — proposed credit: 25% of the Nov 15 usage invoice for the affected routes.
- SLA adjustment: offer a 3-month enhanced SLA (lower latency SLO for embedding endpoints) at no additional cost, plus a dedicated runbook and 30-day retention on audit logs for your account.
- Evidence: we will share the request logs and mapping CSV and produce a short postmortem document.

Attachments on the Drive: request_logs_20271115.log, tenant_quota_mapping.csv, playbook-ratecap-adjustment.pdf. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novagrid-429-post-attach

Please confirm if the credit percentage is acceptable to you and whether Legal Ops should start a formal amendment for the SLA change. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute sync to walk through the postmortem and action items.

Best,
Tessa
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novagrid.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <contracts@novagrid.io>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:10:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s impacting Novagrid - remediation proposal and credit offer

Tessa —

Thanks, that all sounds reasonable. We accept the immediate credit proposal and the temporary SLA uplift — Legal Ops, please coordinate the amendment. A few asks from our side: 
- We need the final reconciliation spreadsheet (per-route counts) by EOD Wednesday so we can reconcile with our billing.
- Can you confirm the exact time range you will use to calculate the credit?

We'll take the 30-minute review on Thursday if you have availability.

—Daniel
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novagrid.io>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 17:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s impacting Novagrid - final reconciliation and closeout

Hi Daniel —

Attached is the reconciliation workbook (novagrid_timelines.xlsx) and the per-route counts we've used for the credit calculation. Summary: the credit was calculated against the affected routes for the period 08:35–10:10 PST on 2027-11-15, prorated to your usage. The credit amount will appear on your December invoice as a line item and we've also opened an amendment request with Legal Ops for the three-month SLA uplift.

Action items completed: 
- Mapping corrected and validated (Ben/infra).
- Dry-run protections added to the sync script (Karthik).
- Alert and dashboards for enforcement drift created and enlisted in oncall runbooks.
- Postmortem draft uploaded to Drive (link above).

If everything looks good on your end we'll mark this incident closed on Friday and follow up with the formal amendment paperwork. Thanks for being responsive during the investigation.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability & Billing, Redwood Inference
